FINDING_ID: Codex_R3_F001  
SEVERITY: 0.91  
FLAW_CLASS: 1  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.72  
DESCRIPTION: `BLIND -> SYNTH` leaves `current_round` at `0` in [bench/dynamic_management.py:1238](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L1238), and `DynamicManager.process_round()` keys detector storage and `RoundResult.round_idx` from `self.fsm.current_round` in [bench/dynamic_management.py:3542](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L3542). So the second processed phase reuses round `0`: blind-round findings get overwritten in `ConvergenceDetector`, and `_round_results` can contain duplicate indices like `[0, 0]`. I reproduced this with a minimal manager run. This is real data loss, not just a missing SYNTH feature.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Separate protocol phase from persisted round number. Either give SYNTH its own non-round handler, or store it under a distinct phase key instead of reusing blind round `0`. Add a test that two successive `process_round()` calls never overwrite blind-round detector data.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: Codex_R3_F002  
SEVERITY: 0.86  
FLAW_CLASS: 1  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.69  
DESCRIPTION: `RoundProgressionFSM.select_event()` can still return `Event.COMPLETE` in `TERMINAL` when `round_complete=True` because it never rejects terminal state up front in [bench/dynamic_management.py:1285](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L1285). `DynamicManager.process_round()` also has no early `is_terminal` guard before mutating detectors in [bench/dynamic_management.py:3577](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L3577). I verified that an extra post-terminal `process_round()` call adds new convergence data before `transition()` finally raises `RuntimeError`. Terminal protection happens too late to protect state.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Make `select_event()` raise immediately when `self.is_terminal` is true, and short-circuit `DynamicManager.process_round()` at the top before any side effects if the FSM is already terminal.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: Codex_R3_F003  
SEVERITY: 0.81  
FLAW_CLASS: 1  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.58  
DESCRIPTION: Config validation allows `max_rounds=1` in [bench/dynamic_management.py:212](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L212), but `SYNTH -> ROUND_1` is unconditional in [bench/dynamic_management.py:1239](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L1239). With `max_round_idx=0`, `ROUND_1` gets neither `COMPLETE` nor `MAX` in `valid_events()` at [bench/dynamic_management.py:1184](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L1184). I reproduced this: the machine enters `ROUND_1` and can no longer finish by normal round exhaustion.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Either require `max_rounds >= 2`, or special-case `max_rounds == 1` so SYNTH exits directly to terminal/max without inventing `ROUND_1`.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: Codex_R3_F004  
SEVERITY: 0.66  
FLAW_CLASS: 8  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.43  
DESCRIPTION: `RoundResult` claims to be the result of a single round in [bench/dynamic_management.py:3316](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L3316), but `process_round()` stores `state=new_state` after the FSM has already advanced in [bench/dynamic_management.py:3736](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L3736). So the record for round `r` describes the next state, not the state that actually ran. That makes audit and replay ambiguous even if round numbering is fixed.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Store both `state_before` and `state_after`, or rename the current field to `post_transition_state` and add the pre-transition state explicitly.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: Codex_R3_F005  
SEVERITY: 0.60  
FLAW_CLASS: 8  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.31  
DESCRIPTION: `DynamicManagementConfig.blind_first` is declared as a HARD Area-3 control in [bench/dynamic_management.py:116](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L116), but it is never read anywhere else in the module. A caller can set `blind_first=False` and the system will still start in `BLIND`, so the config silently misrepresents runtime behavior.  
PROPOSED_FIX: If blind-first is mandatory, validate `blind_first is True` and remove the fake configurability. If it is meant to be configurable, thread it through FSM initialization and transitions and test both modes.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

No other high-confidence missed flaws stood out in this slice; the remaining larger SYNTH-phase design gaps were already reflected in earlier findings.
